claims.text: TaVCrW is a disordered BCC solid solution at 0 K.
Empirical GGA-PBE/LDA underbinding and overbinding rules fail for V and Cr at 0 K.
Short-range order stabilizes solid TaVCrW by approximately 2-3 meV/atom.
An MTP trained on TaVCrW DFT data can replace the EAM reference potential.
Free energy perturbation can replace thermodynamic integration for calculating the TaVCrW solid-liquid free-energy difference.
The substitution is accurate if the MTP reproduces the ab initio phase-space distribution of the solid and complex liquid.
The proposed MTP+FEP method will reduce computational cost by more than 80% relative to TOR-TILD.
The proposed method will reproduce the TOR-TILD free-energy difference to within 0.5 meV/atom.
Reproducing local atomic environments and SRO configurations is the structural mediator that permits accurate FEP sampling.
The MTP is a computationally efficient surrogate for the DFT energy landscape and can generate the large configuration sample required by FEP.
Accurate phase-space sampling by the MTP allows FEP to converge without the extensive integration path used by TI.
Electronic gap effects at the Fermi level can shift the melting point by tens of kelvin.
Accurately reproducing SRO and electronic-gap effects will keep FEP estimates within the sub-meV accuracy threshold.
The MTP+FEP melting temperature for TaVCrW will be within 10 K of the TOR-TILD result.
The range 2000-2400 K is sufficient to sample the melting transition, SRO effects, the liquid, and the solid-liquid coexistence region.
A supercell containing more than 100 atoms is needed to capture the SRO correlation length and validate the 2-3 meV/atom stabilization.
Electronic excitations must be represented in the DFT training set or through post-processing corrections.
High-temperature magnetic fluctuations may materially affect the calculated free energy and therefore must be included or corrected.
TOR-TILD using an EAM reference and thermodynamic integration is computationally expensive.
Functional errors and neglected magnetic fluctuations could propagate into the MTP and produce errors greater than 0.5 meV/atom.

contradictions.description: The conditions require magnetic fluctuations to be included or corrected, while the boundary and uncertainty fields describe them as currently neglected. Thus, the stated implementation does not clearly satisfy one of its own necessary conditions.
